answer: Here is one mechanism that works: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because pulse only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, nadir is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any opal approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
